title: Claude Code Subagents
one_liner: A subagent is a Markdown file that defines a worker with its own context, tools and permissions. Claude delegates to it by description and receives a summary.

core.title: A subagent works in its own context and returns a summary
core.body: Use one when a side task would flood the main conversation with search results, logs or file contents. The subagent does the work separately and returns only the result.
core.why: The main context stays small. Subagent requests still count toward the same usage limits.

quotes.text: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.
quotes.label: Subagents > Overview

quotes.text: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary
quotes.label: Subagents > Overview

core.title: A subagent is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter
core.body: Only `name` and `description` are required. The Markdown body is the system prompt. `tools`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `mcpServers`, `hooks` and `memory` are optional. You can also ask Claude to write the file for you.
core.why: A file without a `name` is treated as documentation, and one without a `description` is skipped.

quotes.text: Subagents are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
quotes.label: Subagents > Quickstart

core.title: The description drives delegation
core.body: Claude compares your request with each subagent's `description`. Include a phrase such as 'use proactively' to encourage delegation. Keep descriptions short; detail belongs in the system prompt.
core.why: Combined descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning. Vague descriptions mean unreliable delegation.

quotes.text: Claude uses each subagent's description to decide when to delegate tasks.
quotes.label: Subagents > Overview

quotes.text: To encourage proactive delegation, include phrases like "use proactively" in your subagent's description field.
quotes.label: Subagents > Automatic delegation

core.title: Scope decides which definition wins
core.body: Managed settings override the `--agents` flag, which overrides project `.claude/agents/`, which overrides user `~/.claude/agents/`, which overrides plugin agents. Commit project subagents so the team shares them.
core.why: A same-named subagent in a higher location silently replaces the lower one.

quotes.text: When multiple subagents share the same name, Claude Code uses the one from the higher-priority location.
quotes.label: Subagents > Choose the subagent scope

core.title: Restrict capabilities with tools and permissions
core.body: A subagent inherits all tools if `tools` is omitted. Use `tools` as an allowlist or `disallowedTools` as a denylist. `permissionMode` sets how permission prompts behave.
core.why: Restricting tools is the main way to make a reviewer read-only and keep it that way.

quotes.text: Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted.
quotes.label: Subagents > Frontmatter reference

quotes.text: Tools to deny, removed from inherited or specified list.
quotes.label: Subagents > Frontmatter reference

core.title: Subagents start in the background by default
core.body: A subagent Claude spawns from the main conversation runs concurrently unless you change it. Foreground subagents block the conversation and pass permission prompts to you. Background ones surface prompts in the main session.
core.why: Do not assume the result is available in the same turn.

quotes.text: With nothing configured, a subagent that Claude spawns from your main conversation starts in the background.
quotes.label: Subagents > Foreground or background

quotes.text: Foreground subagents block the main conversation until complete.
quotes.label: Subagents > Foreground or background

core.title: Choose a subagent only when isolation helps
core.body: Use the main conversation for back-and-forth, shared context across phases, quick edits and low latency. Use a subagent for verbose output, enforced tool limits, or self-contained work that returns a summary.
core.why: A subagent that is not a fork starts fresh and needs time to gather context.

quotes.text: The task produces verbose output you don't need in your main context
quotes.label: Subagents > Subagents or main conversation

quotes.text: The work is self-contained and can return a summary
quotes.label: Subagents > Subagents or main conversation

skip.title: Built-in subagents
skip.note: Explore and Plan start without CLAUDE.md and the git snapshot; other built-ins load both.

skip.title: Model and effort selection
skip.note: `model` and `effort` frontmatter, with a documented model resolution order.

skip.title: Hooks scoped to a subagent
skip.note: Define lifecycle hooks in frontmatter; ignored for plugin subagents.

skip.title: Persistent memory
skip.note: `memory` set to `user`, `project` or `local` enables cross-session learning.

skip.title: Worktree isolation
skip.note: `isolation: worktree` runs the subagent in a temporary git worktree.

skip.title: Nested subagents and limits
skip.note: Up to three layers by default; a limit of 20 concurrent subagents. Both are configurable by environment variable.

skip.title: Forks
skip.note: A fork inherits the conversation, unlike a regular subagent.

skip.title: Resuming subagents
skip.note: A finished or partial subagent can be resumed.

skip.title: Example subagents
skip.note: Code reviewer, debugger, data scientist, database query validator.

practice.title: Create a read-only reviewer
practice.goal: Write a subagent file and see automatic delegation.
steps: Wait a few seconds; Claude Code watches the directory and no restart is needed
Ask: 'Have the code-reviewer subagent look at my recent changes'

code.text:
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for quality and best practices
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
---

You are a code reviewer. Analyze the code and report issues by priority.

practice.check: The review arrives as a summary and the subagent made no edits.
practice.variation: Remove the `tools` line and check whether the subagent can now edit files.

practice.title: Force a specific subagent
steps: Type `@` and select `code-reviewer (agent)` from the typeahead
Add a task, such as 'look at the auth changes'
Repeat with a plain-language request and compare
practice.check: The @-mention always runs that subagent; the plain request leaves the decision to Claude.
practice.variation: Rewrite the description with 'use proactively' and observe whether Claude delegates unprompted.

practice.title: Break a frontmatter field on purpose
steps: In your reviewer file, rename `tools` to `Tools`
Search `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt` for `does not recognize or apply`
practice.check: The debug log names the unrecognised field, and no error appears in the session.
practice.variation: Delete the `description` line and confirm the file is skipped.

gotchas: Field names are camelCase and must match exactly. An unrecognized field is ignored without an error.
A file is skipped silently when it has no `description`, its YAML does not parse, or its opening `---` is not the first line. Check with `--debug`.
A new `agents` directory created mid-session needs a restart. So do edits under `--add-dir` directories.
The `AskUserQuestion` and `EnterPlanMode` tools are removed from every subagent.
Spawning fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached` at 20 running subagents.

cheatsheet.meaning: Stops the subagent after N turns; output is marked partial.
Preloads full skill content into the subagent.
Keep the subagent in the background.
Guarantee a subagent runs for one task.
Run the whole session as that subagent.

recall.q: What do you get back from a subagent?
recall.a: A summary; its working output stays in its own context.

recall.q: Which two frontmatter fields are required?
Two subagents share a name, one in the project and one in your home directory. Which runs?

recall.a: The subagent inherits every tool available to subagents.

recall.q: How do you guarantee a particular subagent runs?
recall.a: @-mention it, or run the session with `--agent`.

recall.q: When should you stay in the main conversation instead?
recall.a: For iterative work, shared context across phases, quick changes, or when latency matters.
